title: UP EARLY, WAITING AT THE EDGE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early in the morning Joshua and all the Israelites set out from Shittim and went to the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over. — Josh 3:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The great moment had come. After forty years of wilderness wandering, Israel finally stood at the edge of the Promised Land. Notice the small detail: "early in the morning." Joshua did not drag his feet or delay. When God is leading forward, faith rises early and gets moving.

But then something interesting happens. They come to the Jordan, and they camp. They stop right at the edge and wait. They do not rush across in their own strength. There is a time to move quickly and a time to wait for God's signal, and wisdom knows the difference.

That riverbank is a picture of many moments in our own lives. We stand at the edge of something new — a decision, a change, a step of obedience — and God says, "Wait here. Not yet." The waiting is not wasted time. It is where our hearts get prepared for what God is about to do.

Israel could not know it yet, but God was about to do something they would never forget. Often our biggest breakthroughs come right after a season of waiting at the edge. Christ Himself waited on the Father's timing in all things (John 7:6), and He teaches us to move promptly when God says go, and to wait patiently when God says wait.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you at the "edge" of something, waiting on God's timing?
2. Do you find it harder to move quickly or to wait patiently?
3. How might God be preparing your heart in a season of waiting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to rise early in obedience and to wait patiently at the edge. Prepare my heart for what You are about to do. Amen.
